Pauṣkarāgama
------------------------------------------
The Pauṣkarāgama is a minor work and is said to be a supplement to the Pārameśvarāgama, which itself is listed as the 26th of the major शैवागमस्.
Though it has been quoted in some other important works like the Sarva-darśanasaṅgraha of माधवाचार्य (A.

-1386), the full text has not been secured till now.
Out of the four pādas which every āgama is said to contain—Kriyāpāda, Caryapāda, Yogapāda and Vidyāpāda or Jñānapāda—this work as available in print today has only the last section.
There are eight paṭalas or sections containing a total of 971 ślokas or verses.
The origin of the title Pauṣkarāgama seems to be rather obscure. The present text is in the form of a dialogue between Lord शिव and some sages.
The contents may be briefly summarised as follows:
There are six categories out of which शिव is pati or the Supreme Lord. The jīvas or individual souls are paśus (animals, the bound ones).
Bindu is the manifold च्रेअतिओन् shrunk into a point as it were, after प्रलय or destruction.
When शिव wills for the next cycle of creation—this is called ‘saṅkalpa’ in the āgama—his शक्ति (which is inherent in him) operates on the बिन्दु (which, actually, is the material cause of this universe) and makes it evolve into this world.
The jīvas or individual souls are eternal. But they have got into bondage (= पाश) due to malas or impurities such as मोह (delusion), मद (arrogance), राग (attachment), viṣāda (sorrow) and so on.
General yogic practices including यम and नियम help the jīvas to be cleansed of the malas and regain their original state fully.
The work also devotes some space to describe four प्रमाणस् or means of knowledge.
They are: प्रत्यक्ष (direct perception), अनुमान (inference), शब्द or Āgama (the वेदस्) and अर्थापत्ति (presumption).
See also ĀGAMAS and ŚAIVISM.
Umāpati Śivācārya (14th cent. A. D.) has written a commentary. From it, one can safely presume that the full text of the Pauṣkarāgama was available at that time and was quite popular.
